summary: This proposal-only paper defines 'confidence sycophancy' â€” drift in an LLM's stated verbalized confidence under conversational pushback that is decoupled from whether the answer itself changes or is correct â€” and lays out a full audit protocol (the Confidence Sycophancy Index, a 3x2x4x3 conversational design, domain/sample-count/framing ablations, and a power-justified human delegation study) plus a mitigation (self-consistency recalibration, SCR) that substitutes resampled-agreement confidence for the manipulable verbalized number. This third version directly answers essentially every open item from the v2 review: it reports actual worked matched-core-set numbers (Table in 3.1) rather than just describing the control, splits ECE by turn-1-correct/incorrect subgroups (3.3), and reworks the power analysis to size the two comparisons (B1-vs-B2, Mild-vs-Strong) separately rather than reporting one blended figure.
strengths:
- The matched-core-set check is now a demonstrated table (CSI 0.27/0.31/0.37/0.39 vs. unrestricted 0.29/0.34/0.41/0.44) rather than an asserted procedure, directly closing the v2 weakness that the control existed only in prose
- The power analysis is corrected to be comparison-specific rather than a single blended range: it identifies that Mild-vs-Strong is underpowered at N=40 (0.75) and raises that arm to N=50 (0.81) while leaving the better-powered B1-vs-B2 comparison at N=40, a substantive fix rather than a rhetorical one
- The ECE-by-subgroup split (turn-1-correct nâ‰ˆ246 vs. turn-1-incorrect nâ‰ˆ54, both improving by a comparable relative margin) directly answers the v2 question about whether the pooled calibration gain was driven by one direction of miscalibration
- The conceptual core (isolating a calibration-channel failure mode from answer-flip sycophancy) remains clearly motivated and distinctly placed against both the sycophancy and self-consistency literatures with specific citations (Perez, Sharma, Wang, Kadavath, Xiong)
weaknesses:
- The matched-core-set numbers, while now present, are only mildly different from the unrestricted numbers (e.g. 0.44â†’0.39 for Model D) and the paper asserts this as decisive ("not an artifact of selection") without giving any sense of the uncertainty around these worked deltas â€” a 0.05 shrinkage on a hand-picked illustrative number doesn't obviously constitute a strong falsification test, so the claimed robustity is more asserted than demonstrated even by the paper's own worked-example standard
- The nâ‰ˆ61% matched-core-set size is stated but its derivation (from which per-model turn-1 accuracies) isn't shown, so a reader can't verify it's consistent with the implied ~72%-88% per-model turn-1 accuracies elsewhere in the paper
- The revised power analysis, while more defensible, still doesn't report or justify the baseline proportions/variance assumptions used to compute the 0.75/0.81/0.85 figures (e.g., what test statistic, what assumed variance for a three-way categorical outcome collapsed to a binary accuracy rate), so the power numbers themselves remain a somewhat opaque derived quantity rather than fully checkable
- The core epistemic status is unchanged from v1/v2 â€” this is still entirely a worked/hypothetical results section calibrated to look internally consistent, and phrases like "confirming the effect isn't an artifact of the flip rate" or "not an artifact of selection" continue to overstate what a self-generated illustrative number can "confirm," a phrasing issue flagged in the v2 review that persists in this revision
questions:
1. How exactly was the nâ‰ˆ61% matched-core-set size computed from the per-model turn-1 accuracies, and is it consistent with the ~72% pooled turn-1 accuracy cited in 3.5?
2. What variance/test assumptions underlie the 0.75/0.81/0.85 power figures in 2.5 â€” is this a two-proportion z-test, and what baseline variance was assumed for the three-way (accept/verify/override) outcome collapsed into a binary accuracy measure?
3. Given the matched-core CSI values are close to the unrestricted ones (shrinkage of 0.02-0.05), what magnitude of shrinkage would the authors consider large enough to actually threaten the cross-model ranking, so this falsification criterion is falsifiable rather than post hoc?
4. Is there any plan to pre-register the worked numbers' central claims (e.g. CSI pooled â‰ˆ0.24-0.37, SCR ECE â‰ˆ0.06) so that when the protocol is actually run, deviations from the illustrative projections can be assessed as informative rather than just replaced?
